findings.claim: canManage() returns hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so an admin with only an all-groups VIEW permission passes the global manage check. This is a VIEW-to-write privilege escalation.
findings.evidence: GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup (GroupsResource.java:181) gates only on auth.groups().requireManage(). A view-only admin can therefore create top-level groups. With rep.id set, they can also re-parent any group to top level via realm.moveGroup(child, null) at GroupsResource.java:198. canManage(GroupModel) at line 78 correctly requires MANAGE only. In V1, canManage() means MANAGE_USERS only. testViewGroups never attempts a write. Reasoned test: createAllGroupsPermission(policy, Set.of(VIEW)), then groups().add(...) should return 403 but returns 201. Not run.
findings.reason: Four seats agree. Two rated it Critical and two Important; normalised to Critical because it is an authorization bypass. The claim is reasoned, not observed, so step 5 must make the 403 test red on the pinned code before fixing (likely hasPermission(null, MANAGE)).

findings.claim: The canManage() Javadoc documents the escalation as the contract: for V2 it says the check passes with a permission to 'VIEW or MANAGE groups'.
findings.evidence: Seats cite GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:75-76 (open-code-review, superpowers), ~72-78 (mattpocock) and ~86 (ponytail). The text copies the canView wording, so it cannot count as intent.
findings.reason: This is a documentation defect separate from the code at GroupPermissionsV2.java:70. Correct it to MANAGE only, together with the canManage() fix.

findings.claim: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() adds groupResource.getId(), which is an authz resource UUID, instead of a group ID. With an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS permission it returns {<Groups type-resource UUID>}, so user search and count come back empty.
findings.evidence: UsersResource.searchForUser (UsersResource.java:398, 425, 430, 448) and BruteForceUsersResource.java:147 pass the set as UserModel.GROUPS. JpaUserProvider (762-765, 1059-1089) then restricts to members of a group with that ID, and none exists. GET /users and /users/count therefore return nothing, although canView(user) would allow every member. V1 adds resource.getName().substring(prefix) instead (GroupPermissions.java:313-315). Reasoned test: all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS, then users().search(null,-1,-1) should contain alice but is empty. Not run.
findings.reason: Four seats agree. One rated it Critical; normalised to Important because it denies visibility rather than escalating access. Reasoned only, so step 5 must make it red first.

findings.claim: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() never collects per-group grants. findByType(server, "Groups") only matches the typed all-groups resource, and hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) looks a resource ID up by name, misses, and falls back to the type resource. With only per-group VIEW_MEMBERS the set is empty.
findings.evidence: Per-group resources are created by resourceStore.create(server, name, owner) without a type (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:121). Only init() sets the type (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:271-274). findResourceIdByType filters on r.type (ResourceEntity.java:64). With an empty set, getUsersCount(realm, emptySet) returns 0 (JpaUserProvider.java:599-602) while /users returns members through the canView post-filter. Count and list disagree, and first/max apply before the post-filter, so pages come back short or empty and the lookup is a full scan. testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers passes only through that post-filter. Reasoned test: per-group VIEW_MEMBERS on topGroup, then users().count() should be 1 but is 0. Not run.
findings.reason: Four seats agree. Its cause (per-group resources never enumerated or matched) differs from the wrong-ID defect at line 123, so it is a separate finding. Reasoned only, so step 5 must make the count test red first.

findings.claim: hasPermission evaluates only the per-group resource when one exists, so all-groups permissions are ignored for any group that has its own permission, including one granted to someone else.
findings.evidence: DefaultPolicyEvaluator adds type-level policies only when resource.getType() != null, and per-group resources have no type. findPolicyIdByNullResourceScope / findByScopes(server, null, ...) exclude policies tied to the type resource. The patch also removed the canViewGlobal short-circuit in GroupsResource.java:113 and GroupResource getSubGroups, so listings depend on this per-group check. UserPermissionsV2 has the same pattern. Reasoned test: all-groups VIEW for myadmin plus per-group permission on topGroup for another user, then topGroup should still be visible.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by two seats, so not reported and not fixed in this loop. Unverified: it rests on reading DefaultPolicyEvaluator and the JPA queries. Settle it with the mixed-permission test. ponytail: track as follow-up.

findings.claim: When the all-groups type resource is evaluated, every per-group permission is pulled in. A per-group grant on group A therefore leaks to every group that has no per-group resource. The Groups copy of hasPermission omits the permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId()) filter that UserPermissionsV2 carries.
findings.evidence: findByResourceType(server, "Groups") (PolicyEntity.java:64) matches defaultResourceType and so returns per-group permissions. DecisionPermissionCollector.onComplete grants scopes without a containsResource check. UserPermissionsV2 added the resource-ID filter in c2acddc7ca for the equivalent user leak. Reasoned test: per-group VIEW on myGroup plus all-groups MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP for another user, then groups().groups() should have size 1 but is expected to return 2.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by two seats. Unverified: ponytail could not read c2acddc7ca and did not prove exploitability. Settle it with the test sketch. ponytail: track as follow-up.

findings.claim: hasPermission is a third near-copy of the evaluator in UserPermissionsV2.java:94-133 and ClientPermissionsV2.java:207-235. It should be a single helper on MgmtPermissionsV2.

findings.claim: Deleting a group under FGAP v2 leaves its per-group authz resource and permissions orphaned.
findings.evidence: The GroupRemovedEvent cleanup is registered only for v1 (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ). v1 and v2 share a feature key and are mutually exclusive. AuthorizationStoreFactory synchronizers cover clients, realms and users only. GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws.
findings.reason: Appendix: two seats. This is a spec gap, possibly planned for later work. ponytail: add v2 group cleanup.

findings.claim: The v1 feature check moved from event time to listener-registration time. When v1 is enabled at runtime, the role/client/group-removed cleanup listener is never registered.
findings.evidence: The legacy testsuite uses @EnableFeature(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, skipRestart = true) (e.g. UsersTest.java:228/235/258/295 and the token-exchange tests). In those runs v1 resources are orphaned. Production is unaffected because Profile is fixed at boot. ponytail and superpowers judged production behaviour unchanged, which does not address the runtime-enable case.
findings.reason: Appendix: two seats. The effect is test-suite-only. ponytail: revisit if the legacy tests leak resources.
